sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: A small evergreen tropical tree, usually no taller than about 5 m but reaching 12 m, with a spreading crown and large obovate leaves. Small flowers grow in panicles and develop into a 2–3 cm kidney-shaped drupe beneath the swollen red or yellow stalk known as the cashew apple. Native to tropical America, it is cultivated throughout the tropics.

sections.title: Food and safety
sections.text: The cashew apple and kernel are eaten. The kernel must be extracted and processed because the shell contains caustic, irritating oil; raw shell material is not edible.
